mainEntity.name: How do ADUs work on multifamily properties in Los Angeles County (duplexes and small apartment buildings)?

acceptedAnswer.text:
Multifamily properties in Los Angeles County often have **broader ADU options**, including multiple conversion ADUs plus newly built units, subject to caps. The rules differ from single‑family lots and can unlock significant extra housing.

Owners can sometimes convert non‑habitable space (storage, boiler rooms, tuck‑under parking) into ADUs and add detached units on the lot. Each jurisdiction sets precise limits based on unit count and zoning.

Key factors:
- Maximum number of conversion ADUs allowed as a percentage of existing units
- Limits on newly constructed detached ADUs on multifamily lots
- Parking, access, and fire separation requirements
- Impact on existing tenants and rent‑controlled units

Have a feasibility study done that maps all existing structures and non‑habitable spaces, then overlays local multifamily ADU rules. Multi‑unit ADU projects benefit from careful phasing and tenant communication.

Contractors with multifamily ADU experience can help you unlock this density without running afoul of safety or tenant regulations.
